questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Academic opportunities

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: Salamanca is a historical university city, and I was seeking an academic challenge. I also wanted to stay in a smaller city, since it's easier to get to know others in a smaller city. I have friends, who study at the University of Salamanca, and they've spoken positively about the city, which encouraged me to apply for my Erasmus.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: It was lovely! I don't regret my decision at all.

questions.question: How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: Somewhat easy. There are quite a lot of international students in Salamanca, and my coordinator was very helpful and always answered my questions whenever needed.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: Mainly from my coordinator, Alejandro Lozano. He helped me answering the questions I had, and helped me change the subjects that I had to change.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: It was quite easy. I booked a room through UniPlaces.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: Since Salamanca is quite small, it's not difficult living off-campus, since everything is within walking distance.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: It was a bit confusing, and they didn't let me register until I had all my papers fixed from Denmark.

questions.question: Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: I had to do the matriculation, after I had recevied my Online Learning Agreement. The matriculation took part mainly online, and I then had to go and get my student ID (which I never received, as they failed to inform me how to get it).

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: Mainly help from my coordinator.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: Quite successful, as my coordinator helped me finding the courses I'd wanted tot take.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Don't hesitate to reach out and ask questions! The coordinators are more than happy to assist you.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: The courses were very intense, and I wasn't aware of the system in Spain with grading. It would've been helpful if I had been better informed beforehand.

questions.question: Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: I had four courses in the 4th year, and one in the second year. The level was somewhat high but quite different from Denmark.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: In Denmark, the professors expect the students to participate in class, and ask critical questions, while in Spain, it's much more about memorizing everything in class, and not asking nearly as many questions. It's more about looking at a PowerPoint, and writing down everything.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer: Theory of Art, Image Aesthetics, Political Philosophy, Cultural Philosophy, History and Tipology of Religions

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: I'd highly recommend Political Philosophy and Cultural Philosophy, as those subjects are fairly more doable than others. The professors are also very open towards Erasmus Students.

questions.answer: There were some presentations and sports activities. I didn't participate in any

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: I'd highly recommend doing the excursions that are offered by the different Erasmus organizations. I went on five trips; one to a nearby village, one to Portugal, one to Seville, one to a hiking area, and one to Bilbao and San Sebastián. It's an excellent opportunity to bond with other international students.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: It was pretty tricky in some ways. The Spanish culture is very different from the Danish one, and Spaniards aren't the most social ones when it comes to foreign students.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Maybe try to join a sports club, where local students are playing. Some local students are more open than others, so definitely try to do some group work with them. Some local students volunteer in different Erasmus organizations and are easier to bond with.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: Definitely that Spaniards aren't very keen on befriending international students. Most of my friends, myself included, had very few local friends.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: Definitely the siesta culture! Having a break in the afternoon is very well-needed, especially when the courses are quite heavy. And I loved the food as well, as well as the outdoor culture.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
1) Consider how you want to live (student dorm, shared apartment...).
2) Have several subjects in mind.
3) It's okay to fail an exam, in most cases you can repeat the exam.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: Don't be afraid to ask questions, the professors and coordinators are there to help you.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: Experiencing growth, both personally and academically!

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: Overcoming cultural boundaries, for sure.

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
